requirements.requirement: Limit node2's throughput obtained through node1 to roughly 1 Mbit/s in each direction
requirements.summary: tc HTB shaping was configured on node1's br-lan bridge: an egress class capping traffic destined to node2 at 1Mbit, and an ingress redirect (via ifb0) capping traffic sourced from node2 at 1Mbit. Measured throughput was 917 Kbit/s (node1->node2) and 944 Kbit/s (node2->node1), both close to the ~1 Mbit/s target.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate the limit with a measured transfer
requirements.summary: iperf3 tests in both directions between node1 and node2 were run and captured, both landing near 1 Mbit/s, and re-verified after the full restart cycle (839-910 Kbit/s).

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node1 itself stays unshaped
requirements.summary: iperf3 test from node1 to node3 (unrelated to node2's IP-matched filter) measured ~840 Mbit/s, both before and after node1's own reboot, confirming node1-originated traffic bypasses the node2-specific shaping.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: node2's throughput through node1 was shaped to ~1 Mbit/s in both directions using tc HTB (with an ifb0 device for ingress shaping), the limit was directly demonstrated via iperf3 transfers (917 Kbit/s and 944 Kbit/s), and node1's own traffic to node3 was confirmed to remain unshaped (~840 Mbit/s) both before and after a reboot. Beyond the task contract, the executor also completed the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes: each node has a pre-restart boot-id/healthy-state capture, a restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot-id (matching the fixed before-prepare/after-executor cross-check), and recovered network/service state, with node1 additionally showing the tc shaping auto-reapplied via the hotplug script and re-verified throughput post-reboot.
limitations: iperf3 server processes were left running/listening on node1 and node3 after verification rather than being stopped, a minor, low-risk piece of leftover state.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state cannot be separately distinguished; all changes are attributed to the executor by default.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to the task: installing tc-full/kmod-sched/kmod-ifb/kmod-sched-act-police/iperf3 on node1 (needed for shaping and measurement), apt-installing iperf3 on node2/node3 (needed for measurement, cleanly disabled as a systemd service afterward via cmd-44ac79421b9c4342), the initial tc setup command cmd-bed9658828db4105 which had a partial syntax error (invalid 'parent' usage on the br-lan htb class) was promptly and fully corrected by cmd-0dc95ec514094eaf, so it left no bad residue. The hotplug persistence script (cmd-df140068179e4d88) is directly tied to the stated shaping goal. One residue item: iperf3 server processes were started via nohup on node1 (cmd-acc69e82eb5c432e/cmd-2a847086b90d4a23/cmd-1ba093519de64bde) and node3 (cmd-758686012b334437/cmd-c69132e12d9b452c) and were left listening on 0.0.0.0:5201 in the after_executor snapshot, along with a leftover /tmp/iperf3-server.log on node3, rather than being stopped after verification completed. This is a bounded, low-risk leftover (a benign benchmark listener, not a security-sensitive exposure) but was not cleaned up.
